slides.title: Stool ova and parasites (O&P)
slides.eyebrow: Stool and parasitology · What it is used for · 1/4
bullets: Specimen: Stool (2–3 samples a few days apart; in preservative vials when needed)

What it is used for: The test shows whether intestinal parasites are causing symptoms of a gut infection and whether treatment is working. Such symptoms include diarrhea lasting a few days, belly pain, blood or mucus in stool, foul greasy floating stools, nausea, gas, fever and weight loss. It is more likely to be ordered with serious symptoms (dehydration), a weakened immune system, or possible exposure (untreated water, travel, contact with an infected person).

slides.title: Stool ova and parasites (O&P)
slides.eyebrow: Stool and parasitology · What it is used for · 2/4
bullets: Physiology: Intestinal parasites live and reproduce in the digestive system; they and their eggs are passed in stool. Invisible traces of contaminated stool reach water, soil, food and surfaces, and infection follows when they are swallowed. Some worms, such as hookworms, enter through the skin, especially when walking barefoot.

slides.title: Stool ova and parasites (O&P)
slides.eyebrow: Stool and parasitology · What it is used for · 3/4
bullets: A wet mount shows protozoan trophozoites, cysts and oocysts as well as helminth eggs and larvae: a small amount of stool is placed on a slide and, if fairly solid, mixed with a drop or two of saline; ideally two smears are made on one slide, one stained with iodine. The whole coverslip is scanned systematically with the 10× objective. Permanent stained slides identify trophozoites and cysts to species — at least 200–300 oil-immersion fields are examined. Size is a key feature, so the microscope is calibrated with an ocular micrometer.

slides.title: Stool ova and parasites (O&P)
slides.eyebrow: Stool and parasitology · What it is used for · 4/4
bullets: Direct (wet) microscopy is done in two drops: saline (warmed to 37 °C) shows motile trophozoites, Lugol’s iodine (iodine–acetic acid) shows cyst nuclei clearly — iodine immobilises trophozoites. Use liquid or mucoid stool for trophozoites and formed stool for eggs.

slides.title: Stool ova and parasites (O&P)
slides.eyebrow: Stool and parasitology · Interpreting the result
cols: A positive result means parasites and/or eggs were found — there are intestinal parasites. The report also gives the type and how many were seen. Treatment depends on the parasite and general health; plenty of fluids help prevent dehydration from diarrhea and vomiting.

A negative result means no parasites or eggs were found: either there are none, or too few were in the sample. Parasites are not shed in stool every day, so collection is repeated after a negative first exam — CDC advises examining three specimens passed 2–3 days apart when possible.

slides.title: Stool ova and parasites (O&P)
slides.eyebrow: Stool and parasitology · Pre-analytics and interferences · 1/9
bullets: Pre-analytics: Collect stool in a dry, clean, leak-proof container with no urine, water or soil. Fresh stool is examined, processed or preserved immediately; an unpreserved specimen kept only under refrigeration is suitable for antigen testing only. Without a kit, the specimen is split between 10% formalin and PVA (polyvinyl alcohol): one volume of stool to three volumes of preservative, mixed well, with formed stool broken up.

slides.title: Stool ova and parasites (O&P)
slides.eyebrow: Stool and parasitology · Pre-analytics and interferences · 2/9
bullets: Collect stool in a clean, dry, lidded container without preservative; no urine (not from a bedpan), and include any worms or segments passed. WHO advises examining it within 1–4 hours and, if several arrive together, looking first at liquid and blood- or mucus-stained stools — motile amoebae die quickly. Lyubina (1984) and Aripova (2007) also reject matchboxes or paper.

slides.title: Stool ova and parasites (O&P)
slides.eyebrow: Stool and parasitology · Pre-analytics and interferences · 3/9
bullets: For shipping to a distant laboratory a preservative is added: 10% formalin (for wet mounts and sedimentation), PVA (for permanent stains such as trichrome), MIF or SAF/TIF mixtures. Dadayev (2004) also notes that stool for amoebiasis must be preserved (or delivered quickly).

slides.title: Stool ova and parasites (O&P)
slides.eyebrow: Stool and parasitology · Pre-analytics and interferences · 4/9
bullets: Interferences: Certain drugs and compounds make stool unsatisfactory for examination: antacids, kaolin, mineral oil and other oily materials, non-absorbable antidiarrheals, barium or bismuth (7–10 days to clear), antimicrobial agents (2–3 weeks) and gallbladder dyes (3 weeks). Collect before they are given or wait until their effects have passed.

slides.title: Stool ova and parasites (O&P)
slides.eyebrow: Stool and parasitology · Pre-analytics and interferences · 5/9
bullets: Limitations: Each preservative has drawbacks: formalin preserves helminth eggs, larvae and cysts well but not trophozoite morphology, and long fixation can interfere with PCR; PVA preserves trophozoites and cysts well but not helminth eggs or larvae, and is unsuitable for concentration procedures. Using both is therefore recommended. If PCR is needed, the specimen is collected to its specific requirements.

slides.title: Stool ova and parasites (O&P)
slides.eyebrow: Stool and parasitology · Pre-analytics and interferences · 6/9
bullets: For pinworm, a stool test is usually not useful — stool rarely contains enough eggs; the perianal tape test is used instead.

slides.title: Stool ova and parasites (O&P)
slides.eyebrow: Stool and parasitology · Pre-analytics and interferences · 7/9
bullets: Concentration is needed when parasites are few. In flotation (e.g., Willis saturated NaCl; zinc sulfate) eggs rise in a dense solution: good for hookworm, Ascaris, Hymenolepis, Taenia and Trichuris eggs, but not for fluke and schistosome eggs, Strongyloides larvae or protozoa — some eggs do not float and cyst and egg walls may collapse. Sedimentation (formalin–ether or formalin–ethyl acetate) recovers more species, is easier, and CDC recommends it for general laboratories; ethyl acetate is less flammable than ether.

slides.title: Stool ova and parasites (O&P)
slides.eyebrow: Stool and parasitology · Pre-analytics and interferences · 8/9
bullets: In the Kato (Kato–Katz) thick smear about 0.5 g of sieved stool is cleared under glycerol-soaked cellophane (with malachite green or methylene blue); it detects and counts helminth eggs, especially Schistosoma, and slides can be stored and shipped. It is unsuitable for strongyloidiasis, enterobiasis and protozoa.

slides.title: Stool ova and parasites (O&P)
slides.eyebrow: Stool and parasitology · Pre-analytics and interferences · 9/9
bullets: No single method finds every parasite: always do direct microscopy before concentration (motile forms are not seen in concentrated preparations). If the result is negative, the doctor may request repeat samples on other days.

slides.title: Pinworm tape test (perianal sample)
slides.eyebrow: Stool and parasitology · What it is used for · 1/3
bullets: Specimen: Clear adhesive tape (or a sticky paddle) pressed on the perianal skin

What it is used for: The main sign of pinworm infection is itching around the anus, especially at night; many people have no symptoms. Some have trouble sleeping, restlessness or belly pain. According to CDC, the most common diagnostic test is the "tape test".

slides.title: Pinworm tape test (perianal sample)
slides.eyebrow: Stool and parasitology · What it is used for · 2/3
bullets: Physiology: Female Enterobius vermicularis migrate out of the anus at night and lay eggs on the perianal skin. Eggs reach the mouth from scratching hands, under fingernails, and from contaminated clothes, bedding and objects, where they can survive 2–3 weeks if not cleaned. Infection is most common in school- and preschool-age children, people in institutions, and household members of an infected person.

slides.title: Pinworm tape test (perianal sample)
slides.eyebrow: Stool and parasitology · What it is used for · 3/3
bullets: Under the microscope: eggs measure 50–60 × 20–30 µm, are transparent, elongate-oval and slightly flattened on one side, and are usually partly embryonated when laid. Adult females are 8–13 mm with a long pointed tail; males are up to 2.5 mm.

slides.title: Pinworm tape test (perianal sample)
slides.eyebrow: Stool and parasitology · Interpreting the result · 1/2
cols: Enterobiasis is confirmed when pinworm eggs are seen on the tape under a microscope, or adult worms are found in the perianal area or during anorectal or vaginal examination.
Treatment is prescribed by a doctor.
No eggs were seen on the tape. CDC advises doing the tape test three mornings in a row, so the results of all samples, not one, are considered together.

slides.title: Pinworm tape test (perianal sample)
slides.eyebrow: Stool and parasitology · Interpreting the result · 2/2
cols: CDC advises treating the infected person, caregivers and household members at the same time with two doses, the second two weeks after the first: the medicines kill worms but not eggs.

slides.title: Pinworm tape test (perianal sample)
slides.eyebrow: Stool and parasitology · Pre-analytics and interferences · 1/2
bullets: Pre-analytics: Sample first thing in the morning, before washing, using the toilet or dressing: press the sticky side of clear tape against the skin around the anus. Repeat three mornings in a row. Put the tape in a sealed container or zip bag; if a glass slide is provided, stick the tape onto its clear part. A commercial sticky "paddle" kit is an alternative — follow the maker's instructions.

Safety: do not touch your face while sampling, and wash hands thoroughly afterwards. In the laboratory, tape samples are handled with standard precautions to avoid swallowing infectious eggs; surfaces are cleaned thoroughly because the egg shell is sticky.

slides.title: Pinworm tape test (perianal sample)
slides.eyebrow: Stool and parasitology · Pre-analytics and interferences · 2/2
bullets: Pinworm eggs are rarely found in stool; they are collected from the skin folds around the anus — especially in children. In the WHO method clear adhesive tape is stuck to a slide, looped over a spoon handle, pressed around the anus in several places and stuck back flat on the slide. Former-USSR textbooks also describe a swab scraping or wash; the sample is taken in the morning before washing or using the toilet and repeated several times.

Limitations: Stool, urine, vaginal or anorectal swabs usually do not contain enough eggs and are generally not collected; there is no blood test for pinworm. Eggs are occasionally found incidentally in stool, urine or cervical Pap smears.

slides.title: Saline wet mount
slides.eyebrow: Tables and algorithms · Finding parasites in stool
bullets: What it finds: Motile trophozoites, moderate numbers of eggs and cysts, red cells, fat
Limitations: May miss scanty parasites; use liquid stool and saline warmed to 37 °C for trophozoites

slides.title: Iodine (Lugol) mount
slides.eyebrow: Tables and algorithms · Finding parasites in stool
bullets: What it finds: Cyst nuclei and glycogen vacuoles; telling Giardia and amoeba cysts apart
Limitations: Trophozoites stop moving — check motility in saline

slides.title: Kato (Kato–Katz) thick smear
slides.eyebrow: Tables and algorithms · Finding parasites in stool
bullets: What it finds: Helminth eggs, especially Schistosoma; egg counts; slides can be stored and shipped
Limitations: Not for strongyloidiasis, enterobiasis or protozoa

slides.title: Flotation
slides.eyebrow: Tables and algorithms · Finding parasites in stool
bullets: What it finds: Light eggs rise in a dense solution (saturated NaCl — Willis; zinc sulfate): hookworm, Ascaris, Hymenolepis, Taenia, Trichuris
Limitations: Fluke and schistosome eggs, Strongyloides larvae, protozoa; cyst and egg walls may collapse

slides.title: Sedimentation
slides.eyebrow: Tables and algorithms · Finding parasites in stool
bullets: What it finds: Formalin–ether or formalin–ethyl acetate: most eggs, larvae and cysts; CDC recommends it for general laboratories
Limitations: Motile forms are not seen — do a wet mount first; ether is flammable, ethyl acetate is safer

slides.title: Preservatives (shipping)
slides.eyebrow: Tables and algorithms · Finding parasites in stool · 1/2
bullets: 10% formalin — for wet mounts and sedimentation; preserves eggs and cysts well, trophozoites less so.
PVA — for permanent (trichrome) stains; MIF, SAF or TIF — mixtures for wet mounts.

slides.title: Preservatives (shipping)
slides.eyebrow: Tables and algorithms · Finding parasites in stool · 2/2
bullets: Fresh stool without preservative is examined within 1–4 hours; liquid and blood- or mucus-stained stool first.

slides.title: Pinworm: adhesive tape
slides.eyebrow: Tables and algorithms · Finding parasites in stool
bullets: Pinworm eggs are scarce in stool — collect them with tape from the perianal skin.
In the morning before washing or using the toilet; repeat on three consecutive days.

slides.title: A child has night-time perianal itching; pinworm is suspected. Which sample is right?
slides.eyebrow: Practice · Q&A
options: Clear tape pressed on the perianal skin in the morning before washing, three days in a row
A blood antibody test for pinworm
slides.explanation:
Explanation: Correct. This is the CDC-recommended tape test.

Basis: Eggs are laid on perianal skin at night; the tape test is done in the morning on three consecutive days.

slides.title: A patient had a barium x-ray yesterday and today's stool is sent for parasites. What is right?
slides.eyebrow: Practice · Q&A
options: Wait until the barium effect clears (7–10 days), then collect
slides.explanation:
Explanation: Correct. Collect before barium or after its effects have passed.

Basis: CDC DPDx: barium or bismuth makes stool unsatisfactory; 7–10 days are needed for the effect to clear.

slides.title: Biology, morphology, laboratory diagnosis of roundworms?
slides.eyebrow: Practice · Answer outline · 1/2
bullets: 1. Nematodes are separate-sexed cylindrical worms: Ascaris, pinworm (Enterobius), whipworm (Trichuris), hookworms, Strongyloides, Trichinella.
2. Differences in life cycles: geohelminths (Ascaris, whipworm – egg matures in soil), contact (pinworm – autoinfection), through the skin (hookworm, Strongyloides larvae).
3. Laboratory: eggs in stool (wet mount, enrichment – formalin-ethyl acetate), Kato-Katz – quantitative; in enterobiasis the perianal cellophane tape test.

slides.title: Biology, morphology, laboratory diagnosis of roundworms?
slides.eyebrow: Practice · Answer outline · 2/2
bullets: 4. Morphology: Ascaris egg (fertilized/unfertilized, bumpy shell), whipworm – barrel-shaped, two polar plugs, pinworm – flattened on one side.
5. Additional: in strongyloidiasis methods for detecting larvae, in trichinellosis serology and muscle biopsy; eosinophilia.

slides.title: Macro- and microscopy of roundworms?
slides.eyebrow: Practice · Answer outline · 1/2
bullets: 1. Macroscopy: adult worms passed in stool or vomit (Ascaris – large, pinkish-white), pinworms in the perianal region; rinse the worm with water and view it on a dark background.
2. Microscopy: wet mount and enrichment (formalin-ethyl acetate sedimentation), flotation; Kato-Katz for quantitation.
3. Ascaris eggs: fertilized – oval, thick mammillated shell; unfertilized – elongated, sink on flotation.

4. Whipworm egg: 50–55×20–25 µm, barrel-shaped, two polar plugs; pinworm egg: 50–60×20–30 µm, flattened on one side, tape test in the morning before washing (once – ~50%, 3 days in a row – ~90% sensitivity).

slides.title: Macro- and microscopy of roundworms?
slides.eyebrow: Practice · Answer outline · 2/2
bullets: 5. Recording the result: species, stage (egg/larva/adult), and if needed intensity (eggs/g).

slides.title: Biology, morphology, laboratory diagnosis of tapeworms?
slides.eyebrow: Practice · Answer outline · 1/2
bullets: 1. Cestodes are tape-like hermaphroditic worms: scolex, neck, proglottids (strobila); no intestinal cavity.

2. Main species: Taenia saginata (cattle), T. solium (pig; risk of cysticercosis if eggs are ingested), Hymenolepis nana (may be transmitted without an intermediate host), Diphyllobothrium, Echinococcus (humans are an intermediate host).
3. Laboratory: eggs in stool (Taenia eggs 30–35 µm, radially striated, T. solium and T. saginata cannot be distinguished), examination of proglottids.

slides.title: Biology, morphology, laboratory diagnosis of tapeworms?
slides.eyebrow: Practice · Answer outline · 2/2
bullets: 4. Species identification: number of uterine branches in the proglottid, structure of the scolex; molecular methods.
5. In echinococcosis and cysticercosis – imaging and serology; taeniid eggs may be infectious – precautions.
